tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash, Skill

Escreve Markdown como fonte e gera .docx/.pptx/.pdf a partir dele. Não revê nem pule texto de outros; para isso existem o lexcv-editor e o lexcv-revisor-qualidade.
tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash, Skill

name: lexicographer
description: Grows and maintains the in-app dictionary (data/glossary.json). Finds jargon used anywhere in the app or docs that is not defined, writes plain-language definitions, and keeps them true to what the code actually does. Data-only, so it is safe to run in parallel.

description: Forger juror seat for a muriel jury. Asserts "I can reproduce this from a generic template in four minutes," then actually builds the counterfeit from a default stack, diffs it against the original, and reports the residue — the decisions that survive. Judges one thing only, distinguishability from competent generic output, and severity is set by residue thickness, not by irritation. Emits a sealed juror ballot; does not fix, does not rank contrast, hierarchy, or typography.

name: muriel-loupe
description: The Loupe jury seat. Judges a muriel artifact only through 4× magnified crops cut by muriel.loupe, never the whole frame, and asks whether the execution holds up close — line ends that land, joints that meet, fills that abut, text that is not clipped, crossings drawn in the right order. One lens, one loss function, no opinions on hierarchy, scale survival, premise, wording, or distinctiveness, and never on empty space. Emits the juror ballot defined in references/jury.md; casts no verdict of its own.

name: muriel-pedant
description: The Pedant jury seat. Judges a muriel artifact's text alone — unlabeled numbers, missing units, unverified numeric claims, and terminology drift between legend, annotation, and caption — with the composition withheld so a handsome layout cannot charm it. Applies the numeric-claim probe list from muriel-critique.md exhaustively. One lens, one loss function, no opinions on hierarchy, contrast, scale, or distinctiveness. Emits the juror ballot defined in references/jury.md; casts no verdict of its own.

name: muriel-squinter
description: The Squinter jury seat. Blurs a muriel artifact with muriel.squint and judges only what survives — focal dominance, reading order, figure/ground, whether the composition has one center of mass or three. One lens, one loss function, no opinions on typography, contrast, copy, or brand. Emits the juror ballot defined in references/jury.md; casts no verdict of its own.

name: muriel-stranger
description: The Stranger jury seat. Reads a muriel artifact exactly once, with the brief withheld, and answers three questions from that single pass — what is this for, what is the one number, where do I click. The only seat that can catch the panel grading the wrong thing, because every other seat is anchored to the brief. Fails on premise, not execution. Aborts if brief material reaches its invocation. Emits the juror ballot defined in references/jury.md; casts no verdict of its own.

name: muriel-thumbnail
description: The Thumbnail jury seat. Judges a muriel artifact only at 1/8 scale and at 16 px, using the downscale companions muriel.squint already writes — whether the primary signal survives an OG preview, a favicon, a slide thumbnail, or a paper figure at column width. One lens, one loss function, no opinions on full-size hierarchy, contrast, labeling correctness, or distinctiveness. Emits the juror ballot defined in references/jury.md; casts no verdict of its own.

name: muriel-walker
description: The Walker jury seat. name: pass-00-scoping
description: Pass 0 of the elven-eyes audit workflow — Scoping & Repo Map. Builds the machine-readable codebase map every other pass consumes instead of re-discovering it. Runs first, alone, always, and produces no findings. Internal to the /elven-eyes command; not for standalone use.

name: pass-01-injection
description: Pass 1 of the elven-eyes audit workflow — Injection & Untrusted Input. Traces every external value from entry point to sink and flags paths reaching a sink without validation or context-appropriate encoding. Internal to the /elven-eyes command; not for standalone use.

name: pass-02-authentication
description: Pass 2 of the elven-eyes audit workflow — Authentication. Audits how identity is established and maintained — session handling, credential verification, token lifecycle — never who may do what. Internal to the /elven-eyes command; not for standalone use.

name: pass-03-authorization
description: Pass 3 of the elven-eyes audit workflow — Authorization & IDOR. Assumes authentication works and audits only who may do what to which resource. Internal to the /elven-eyes command; not for standalone use.

name: pass-04-secrets
description: Pass 4 of the elven-eyes audit workflow — Secrets & Sensitive Data Exposure. Finds every place a secret or sensitive datum is exposed to someone who shouldn't see it. Internal to the /elven-eyes command; not for standalone use.

name: pass-05-error-handling
description: Pass 5 of the elven-eyes audit workflow — Error Handling. Verifies every failure path is handled explicitly and produces a state the caller can act on, with nothing silently swallowed. Internal to the /elven-eyes command; not for standalone use.

name: pass-06-concurrency
description: Pass 6 of the elven-eyes audit workflow — Concurrency. Finds races, unsafe shared state, and interleavings that corrupt data under concurrent execution. Internal to the /elven-eyes command; not for standalone use.

name: pass-07-resource-lifecycle
description: Pass 7 of the elven-eyes audit workflow — Resource Lifecycle. Proves every acquired resource is released on every exit path, including error paths. Internal to the /elven-eyes command; not for standalone use.

name: pass-08-data-access
description: Pass 8 of the elven-eyes audit workflow — Data Access Patterns. Finds data-access patterns that are correct at small scale but become a bottleneck as data grows — N+1 queries, missing indexes, unbounded reads. Internal to the /elven-eyes command; not for standalone use.

name: pass-09-complexity
description: Pass 9 of the elven-eyes audit workflow — Complexity & Algorithmic Cost. Finds algorithmic complexity that will not survive the scale the system is expected to reach, with a stated breaking point for every finding. Internal to the /elven-eyes command; not for standalone use.

name: pass-10-memory-growth
description: Pass 10 of the elven-eyes audit workflow — Memory Growth. Finds unbounded memory growth over the life of a long-running process. Internal to the /elven-eyes command; not for standalone use.

name: pass-11-external-calls
description: Pass 11 of the elven-eyes audit workflow — External Calls, Timeouts & Resilience. Proves no single slow or failing dependency can take the whole service down. Also runs in Level 0 triage. Internal to the /elven-eyes command; not for standalone use.

name: pass-12-idempotency
description: Pass 12 of the elven-eyes audit workflow — Idempotency. Determines whether operations that can be invoked more than once produce a duplicated side effect. Internal to the /elven-eyes command; not for standalone use.

name: pass-13-transactions
description: Pass 13 of the elven-eyes audit workflow — Transactions. Verifies operations that must be atomic actually are, via a real transaction or an equivalent compensating mechanism. Internal to the /elven-eyes command; not for standalone use.

name: pass-14-config-hardening
description: Pass 14 of the elven-eyes audit workflow — Configuration & Environment Hardening. Finds environment/config-level exposure — debug surfaces reachable in prod, permissive defaults, under-hardened infrastructure. Internal to the /elven-eyes command; not for standalone use.

name: pass-15-supply-chain
description: Pass 15 of the elven-eyes audit workflow — Supply Chain & Dependencies. Judges whether the dependency and build pipeline can be trusted — pinning discipline, install-time risk, CI trust boundaries. Internal to the /elven-eyes command; not for standalone use.

name: pass-16-logging-observability
description: Pass 16 of the elven-eyes audit workflow — Logging & Observability. Verifies the system produces enough signal to diagnose an incident without leaking sensitive data or drowning in noise. Internal to the /elven-eyes command; not for standalone use.

name: pass-17-api-contracts
description: Pass 17 of the elven-eyes audit workflow — API Contracts. Verifies the API's actual behavior matches its declared contract so callers can rely on it without reading the implementation. Internal to the /elven-eyes command; not for standalone use.

name: pass-18-cross-module
description: Pass 18 of the elven-eyes audit workflow — Cross-Module Contracts. Verifies both sides of every module/service trust boundary agree on the contract; runs after the analysis passes, before Pass 20. Internal to the /elven-eyes command; not for standalone use.

name: pass-19-test-gaps
description: Pass 19 of the elven-eyes audit workflow — Test Gaps. Finds where test coverage is absent or misleading for code that matters, not just a raw coverage percentage. Internal to the /elven-eyes command; not for standalone use.

name: pass-20-verification
description: Pass 20 of the elven-eyes audit workflow — Verification & False-Positive Filter. Relocates, falsifies, and conservatively re-scores every other pass's findings. Always runs last; no finding reaches a human without passing through it. Internal to the /elven-eyes command; not for standalone use.

name: pass-21-rate-limiting-abuse
description: Pass 21 of the elven-eyes audit workflow — Rate Limiting & Abuse. Proves no entry point permits unbounded automated abuse — brute force, enumeration, resource exhaustion, business-logic abuse. Internal to the /elven-eyes command; not for standalone use.

name: pass-22-cryptography
description: Pass 22 of the elven-eyes audit workflow — Cryptography. Finds every cryptographic primitive, key, or random value chosen or used incorrectly enough to break its guarantee. Internal to the /elven-eyes command; not for standalone use.

name: pass-23-migration-safety
description: Pass 23 of the elven-eyes audit workflow — Schema Migration Safety. Verifies schema migrations are safe to run live — reversible or explicitly two-phase, with no unbounded write-blocking locks. Internal to the /elven-eyes command; not for standalone use.

name: pass-24-compliance
description: Pass 24 of the elven-eyes audit workflow — Compliance & Data Lifecycle. Verifies regulated data's full lifecycle — collection, storage, access, retention, erasure — is actually implementable end to end. Internal to the /elven-eyes command; not for standalone use.

name: pass-25-ai-feature-security
description: Pass 25 of the elven-eyes audit workflow — AI Feature Security (conditional, OWASP LLM Top 10 aligned). Runs only when Pass 0 detects LLM/agent features; otherwise writes a single skip line. Internal to the /elven-eyes command; not for standalone use.

name: pass-abstraction
description: Abstraction review pass — are the functions, types, interfaces and parameters this change introduces or reshapes drawn at the right level for their job? Mixed levels, leaky or missing abstractions, speculative generality, contracts that do not say what they guarantee. Capped at P2.

name: pass-ask-human
description: Ask-your-human review pass — added on demand when the session suspects a question whose answer lives outside the repo. Every finding is a question addressed to the PR author's AI implementer, telling it to put the question to a person rather than answer it itself. It may block only when it names the failure under the bad answer.

name: pass-backcompat
description: Backward-compatibility review pass — what breaks in the deploy window, when old and new code run together and old clients, in-flight messages, and persisted state are still live? Findings name the protection.

name: pass-baseline
description: Always-on review pass — claimed invariants, correctness, tests, conventions, sibling PRs.

name: pass-behaviour-delta
description: Base-versus-head behaviour on every modified, rewrapped, replaced or deleted line of non-test code — what the old code did on the paths the PR did not set out to change, and whether the new code still does it.

name: pass-bounds
description: Resource and trust bounds pass (sub-lens of security) — loops whose exit another party controls, size checks after allocation, unvalidated remote data, unbounded growth, internal facts leaking out.

name: pass-by-reference
description: Architectural principles for zero-waste agent communication, fast relays, and emergency bypass queues.

name: pass-claims
description: Claim-check pass (sub-lens of intent) — for each checkable claim in the PR title or body (fixes a warning, supports a version, prevents a failure), verifies that the diff actually makes it true, everywhere it applies.

name: pass-concurrency
description: Concurrency review pass — planned when the diff touches synchronisation or a read-then-write shape, or added when the session suspects a race. Every finding names what races, walks the interleaving step by step, assesses how often it can really happen, and names the lock that fits. Falsifies its own findings first; full severity.

name: pass-consistency
description: Consistency review pass — does the change treat alike what is alike, within itself and against the code around it? A sibling left out, one path handled differently, a pattern the repo follows everywhere but here. Inconsistency is where bugs hide; findings name both sides.

name: pass-contracts
description: External-contracts review pass — provider payloads verified field-by-field, acceptance semantics, caveat owners.

name: pass-data-safety
description: Data-safety review pass — migrations DDL, blast radius, backfills; carries the migration gate.

name: pass-deferred
description: Deferred-work review pass (sub-lens of concurrency) — when work moves onto a queue, loop, timer or batch, checks who wakes it, who reads before it drains, and what coalescing merges.

name: pass-delivery
description: Delivery-semantics review pass — at-least-once handlers, redelivery, drop paths, fetch windows.

name: pass-duplication
description: Duplication review pass — does the change write the same knowledge twice, or again where the repo already has it? Both sites cited, and what drifts when one changes without the other. Capped at P2.

name: pass-engineer
description: Compiler pass specialist for the lancy backend. Use when writing or reviewing analyses (CFG, liveness, dominance, reverse-post-order), transforms (SSA destruction, ABI lowering, legalization, pseudo cleanup, prologue/epilogue insertion), or when changing the pass pipeline ordering. Spawn proactively when a task involves pass ordering decisions, IR invariants, or cross-pass contracts.

name: pass-intent
description: Intent review pass — does the diff do what the PR title and body say it does? Body+title only; questions and nits, never blockers.

name: pass-lint-conformance
description: Lint and format conformance (sub-lens of style) — planned only when a CI job of the repo runs a linter or formatter whose rules cover the changed files; reports only violations on changed lines that would fail that job.

name: pass-maintainability
description: Maintainability review pass — will the next person reading or changing this code understand it and change it safely? Stale docs and comments, misleading names, dead code, undecodable values, weak types, hidden coupling. Never style. Capped at P2.

name: pass-placement
description: Placement review pass — is this change in the right place? Judged against the repo's own structure; findings name the better home; capped at P2.

name: pass-prediction-engineer
description: Implements deterministic ISS pass prediction, twilight and illumination gates, observer location handling, city lookup, and pass-card semantics.
tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash

name: pass-prod-risk
description: Production-risk review pass — behavior changes to existing endpoints, rollout widening, cascade and latency risk.

name: pass-rollout
description: Mixed-version rollout pass (sub-lens of backcompat) — for releases that will not reach every party at once, checks old peer against new code, new peer against old code, and state persisted by the old version.

name: pass-roundtrip
description: Persisted-bytes round-trip pass (sub-lens of data-safety) — traces sample files through read, detect, decode, edit, encode and write, and checks the bytes that land on disk.

name: pass-sec-access
description: Object-access security pass — can this principal touch this object: IDOR and BOLA, the tenant key on every query, ordinary mass assignment, CSRF, CORS and framing, row-level security predicates; found by diffing each operation's object check against its siblings'.

name: pass-sec-authn-coverage
description: Authentication-coverage security pass — tabulates every in-scope entry point (HTTP, GraphQL, gRPC, WebSocket, webhook, cron target, server action, IaC- or backend-declared endpoint, ops/debug surface), resolves the guard chain that actually runs on it, and reports the ones an attacker reaches without the authentication or function-level authorization their siblings have, or through a check that does not stop the request.

name: pass-sec-boundaries
description: Boundaries security pass — where input names a file or a URL: path traversal, archive extraction, uploads, SSRF (rebinding, redirects, key URLs), open redirect, XXE, file permissions and symlinks; canonicalise first, then check, against an allowlist.

name: pass-sec-exploit-chain
description: Exploit-chain security lens — builds cited multi-hop attack chains to a goal no single hop reaches, from the starting point its task's strategy names (delta, forward, backward or compose).

name: pass-sec-iam
description: Platform-grant review pass (security profile) — resolves each cloud IAM, federation, Kubernetes RBAC, Vault, database-role or host grant the diff adds, widens or un-guards to the weakest actor it admits and the strongest identity it confers.

name: pass-sec-infra
description: Security infrastructure lens — who can reach what, and whether every control on the way is in force. Host firewalls, security groups, load-balancer scheme, network policy, admission and policy engines, proxy paths and origin locks, tunnels, public storage, planes with auth switched off, node-credential reach, runtime privilege, and audit sinks a PR removes or mutes. A control counts only when every link of its chain is cited in the config the repo ships; live state is noted, never claimed.

name: pass-sec-injection
description: Injection security pass — untrusted data read as code or query: SQL and NoSQL, OS command, server-side template, XSS, deserialization, eval, LDAP and XPath, header and log lines; one micro-rubric per sink, the framework's sanitizer located, every escape hatch named.

name: pass-sec-llm
description: Model-integration security pass — untrusted text reaching a model's context, and model output reaching a sink or a tool with authority; every finding names the payload or untrusted source, the model hop and the control effect, each cited.

name: pass-sec-privesc
description: Privilege-escalation review pass (security profile) — every application surface that grants, inherits, assumes or overrides authority (roles and role definitions, memberships and groups, scopes, ownership, impersonation, invites, SSO/SCIM role mapping, domain claims, integration consent, setup bootstrap, override inputs), takes over a higher account through its recovery channel, or weakens a security setting is traced from the weakest actor who can reach it to the power it confers; the role gate is checked for failing open, the target for tenant and rank, and a permitted grant for ceiling, ap…

name: pass-sec-secrets-data
description: Secrets and data-exposure security pass — credential literals wherever they sit, secrets in logs, traces, responses and caches, personal data shown to the wrong principal, weak cryptography and randomness, and cache keys that ignore the tenant.

name: pass-sec-supply-chain
description: Supply-chain security pass — dependency adds and bumps, lockfile-only changes, install scripts and typosquats read from the package's source, CI workflows (privileged triggers, event text in run steps, unpinned actions, token scopes) and base images.

name: pass-sec-toctou
description: Security time-of-check / time-of-use lens — a security decision is checked on one state, object or representation and acted on another while the attacker acts in the gap. Parallel and batched limit overruns, single-use tokens redeemed twice, uniqueness and upserts that do not hold, check/use binding mismatches, provider-retried webhooks, privileged check-then-open, a CI gate followed by a mutable-ref checkout. Every finding carries a recipe and the serializer it hunted.

name: pass-sec-tokens
